rules.statement: Do not add a request count or latency instrument for HTTP endpoints; enrich ASP.NET Core's `http.server.request.duration` with extra attributes through `IHttpMetricsTagsFeature` instead.
rules.why: A second instrument for the same fact doubles the series a deployment pays for and drifts from the built-in one.
rules.check: New Counter/Histogram recording per-request counts or durations in endpoint or middleware code, instead of tags added via IHttpMetricsTagsFeature.

rules.statement: Count an auditable domain outcome by publishing an event through the event seam, not with a separate counter at the call site; give direct instruments only to hot- or flood-path mechanisms that are not events.
rules.why: A parallel counter drifts from the event count, and sending a flood of refusals through the event pipeline would put back the load the limiter exists to shed.
rules.check: Counter.Add calls next to event publishing for the same outcome, or rate-limit refusals and other flood-path mechanisms published as events.

rules.statement: Every metric attribute value must come from a vocabulary the server controls, never from request input; map an unrecognized value to `_OTHER`.
rules.why: If request input can set an attribute value, any caller can create series at will and exhaust the backend's series limit.
rules.check: Tag values taken from request parameters (grant_type, client_id, headers, URIs) without first checking them against a registered set.

rules.statement: Never use tenant, client, subject, or remote address as metric attributes; put them on traces and logs instead.
rules.why: These values are unbounded and grow with the customer base until the metrics backend drops data.
rules.check: Metric tags, or event metric attributes, holding a tenant id, client id, subject, IP address, or similar per-customer identifier.

rules.statement: Create meters through `IMeterFactory`, never `new Meter(...)`, with one meter per package named after the package and exposed as a public constant.
rules.why: The factory scopes meters to their service provider, so two hosts in one process don't share instruments and tests can read them with `MetricCollector<T>`.
rules.check: `new Meter(` in library code, or a meter name that is a hard-coded literal instead of a public constant matching the package name.

rules.statement: Define a package's instruments once, in one internal singleton metrics class, and have call sites call methods on that class instead of Meter or instrument APIs.
rules.why: This keeps each instrument defined once, in the package that owns the mechanism.
rules.check: CreateCounter/CreateHistogram or Instrument.Add/Record calls scattered across call sites outside the package's metrics class.

rules.statement: Give instrument and attribute names the family namespace prefix (`ncode.{product}.{area}...`), but keep the standard name for attributes that OpenTelemetry semantic conventions already define (such as `error.type`, `http.route`, `http.response.status_code`).
rules.why: Follows ASP.NET Core's naming practice and lets a host subscribe to the whole family with one wildcard.
rules.check: New instrument or attribute names without the family prefix, or custom renames of attributes the semantic conventions already define.

rules.statement: Use UCUM units: durations are histograms in seconds (`s`) with explicit bucket advice, and counts use an annotation unit such as `{request}`.
rules.why: The decision makes UCUM units the convention for every instrument.
rules.check: Duration instruments in ms, or without bucket advice, or counters with no unit or a non-annotation unit.

rules.statement: Library packages must depend only on `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` for instrumentation, not on the OpenTelemetry API or SDK; leave OpenTelemetry wiring to host composition.
rules.why: A library that depends on the SDK forces it on every consumer, and recording costs nothing until a listener subscribes.
rules.check: OpenTelemetry package references or usings in library (non-host) projects.

rules.statement: Add the OTLP exporter only to the specific signal pipeline that needs it, and only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is configured; do not use the cross-signal `UseOtlpExporter`.
rules.why: A host without a collector should not keep retrying a missing endpoint, and `UseOtlpExporter` also exports every log, turns on tracing, and cannot be combined with a host's own exporters.
rules.check: `UseOtlpExporter()` calls, or an OTLP exporter added without checking that the endpoint is configured.

rules.statement: Configure a view that drops unbounded attributes such as `server.address` and `server.port` from `System.Net.Http` instruments when outbound calls go to URIs registered by clients.
rules.why: Hosts of client-registered URIs are unbounded, so they create unbounded series.
rules.check: OpenTelemetry metrics setup that adds System.Net.Http meters without a view filtering out server.address and server.port.

rules.statement: Give every new or changed instrument a unit test that reads it through `MetricCollector<T>` and asserts its name, unit, and attributes, and update the metrics catalog document in the same change.
rules.why: Dashboards and alerts are built against a reviewed contract, so adding or renaming an instrument or attribute must be a deliberate change.
rules.check: A new or renamed instrument or attribute with no MetricCollector test and no update to the metrics catalog doc.

rules.statement: Set the OAuth error-code metric attribute where the error response is written, so every path that writes an error tags it the same way.
rules.why: HTTP status alone cannot tell error codes such as `invalid_grant` and `invalid_client` apart, and tagging in one place keeps every path consistent.
rules.check: An error response path (filter, executor, redirect) that writes an OAuth error without the error attribute, or that tags it somewhere other than the shared writer.
